hero.headline: Stuart downtown dock to close July 6 for $3 million renovation, nearly doubling boat slip capacity
hero.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will shut down July 6 to begin a $3 million renovation project that is scheduled to be finished by next Fourth of July. The year-long improvement will significantly increase the facility's capacity, growing from 18 boat slips to 44 slips that will accommodate both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will consist of a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. The project is being funded through a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Beyond simply adding more space, the upgrades are designed with storm resilience in mind. Mayor Sean Reed explained that the improvements aim to prevent damage during hurricanes and major storms. The dock currently serves more than 1,400 boaters each year, making the expansion a significant investment in the city's waterfront infrastructure. The enhanced capacity will address crowding issues that frequently occur during busy weekends when businesses and boaters struggle to find available spots at the current facility.

The city has worked proactively to minimize disruption to businesses that depend on the dock during the construction period. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates passenger boarding services from the dock, initially faced uncertainty about whether it could continue operations. However, the city found a solution by allowing the business to construct a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the dock. This arrangement will enable Tiki Taxi & Cruises to continue boarding passengers throughout the renovation period. Austin Kuyrkendall, the company's director of operations, expressed relief that the city located a workable compromise.

Local boaters and business operators have embraced the renovation plans. Boat captain Parker Fisher, based in Stuart, acknowledged that the dock needed improvements and welcomed the city's investment. Kuyrkendall emphasized the dock's central importance to Stuart's identity and economy, noting that the modernization project represents more than just a practical upgrade. He described the expansion as beneficial not only for Stuart's water-dependent businesses but also for the community's character and livelihood. The project reflects the city's commitment to enhancing infrastructure while supporting the waterfront businesses and recreational boaters that define Stuart's relationship with its waterways.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Zoning Commission recommends denial of controversial data center near Arden and Saddle View Elementary
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddle View Elementary School. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

One of the central issues during Thursday's hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Board members said they were not presented with enough evidence to conclude the facility would meet that standard. Residents raised concerns about potential health, safety, environmental and noise impacts. Resident Laura Cole voiced concerns about noise generated by large-scale data centers, saying the low-frequency hum penetrates glass and concrete. Project developer Ernie Cox said he was disappointed by the board's recommendation but plans to use the feedback from Thursday's hearing to strengthen his case before county commissioners.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances plan for Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation. The land will support construction of a partial interchange where Midway Road meets Florida's Turnpike. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the interchange is designed to improve accessibility and help the city manage growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

The interchange is part of FDOT's $95 million Midway Road Widening Project, which focuses on reducing congestion and improving safety in the area. Currently, crews are working on the first phase, which involves widening Midway Road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second widening phase, extending from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction expected to begin in summer 2027. The partial interchange itself is also still in the design phase. As part of the overall project, FDOT is also working on improvements to the Turnpike bridge.

Samples explained that the interchange addresses a notable gap in Turnpike access within Port St. Lucie. Currently, there is limited access to Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. Beyond the interchange, the project will include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks to improve connectivity for all users. Port St. Lucie resident Erin Scheumeister acknowledged the impact of the construction but views it as worthwhile. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," she said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work."

The city council will vote on final approval to transfer the land at a future meeting. Samples emphasized that the infrastructure improvements are essential both for the growth that has already transformed Port St. Lucie and for future development planned in the area. While residents like Scheumeister have noticed the ongoing construction, there is general recognition that these projects will benefit the community by easing traffic flow and improving access to major transportation routes as the region continues to grow.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit company proposes elevated system connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: California-based Glydways will present to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday a proposal for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles to connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The system would also link the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept functions like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without traffic or intermediate stops. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport, and one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

The company describes the elevated guideway as resembling a narrow pedestrian bridge rather than a traditional highway structure, with stations potentially integrated into buildings to shield riders from heat and rain. Gettinger said the system would cost a small fraction of traditional light rail systems, which have carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile in previous South Florida discussions. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. The service would be priced like public transit rather than private rideshare. Tuesday's County Commission meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

cards.headline: Delray Beach golf training center delayed 3 months, costs $90,000 after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tee Box, a virtual golf training center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, was delayed three months after problems with a licensed contractor required all work to be redone.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, faced significant delays and costs after contractor problems. The project was originally scheduled to open in April but was delayed three months until July 17. Molen said the contractor constantly postponed work and ultimately failed to complete it properly. Even though the contractor was licensed, the work had to be redone, resulting in approximately $90,000 in additional costs. The estimate does not include lost revenue during delays or expenses for bringing in another contractor. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," Molen said.

David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, said contractor-related issues are impacting many people across Palm Beach County, with an estimated 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners facing major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. According to Allan, the most common contractor complaints in Palm Beach County involve roofing, windows, and air conditioning work. Despite the setbacks, Molen said he is moving forward with his business. "Like the game of golf, I gotta put that bad shot behind me," he said.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran's roof lien removed after contractor dispute resolved
cards.teaser: A Lantana homeowner and disabled veteran saw a nearly $7,000 lien removed from his home and roof repairs completed after a television station intervened in a dispute with Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. McCoy made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company. He said he was mostly satisfied with the work except for two holes left unfinished on the back of his home. McCoy said the company stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails between January and February. Screenshots showed he heard back from a worker on Feb. 5 who said the owner would call, but McCoy said the owner never did.

Letters from Gulfeagle Supply then arrived warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien on McCoy's home. The lien document stated Gulfeagle Supply furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid for those supplies. McCoy said he worried he would have to hire an attorney or go to court at a cost of thousands of dollars. After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized was delivered to McCoy within an hour, removing the lien from his home. The contractor also sent someone back to fix the two problem areas on McCoy's roof.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue 2 from sinking boat in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit rescued two boaters after their small motorized boat took on water and became submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies and their decision to wear life jackets. The Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said in a Facebook post that the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life, and expressed gratitude that the call ended safely and pride in the swift response by their Marine Unit deputies.

cards.headline: California transit company proposes elevated self-driving network connecting downtown West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, with the project going before Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The company, which already has projects underway in Atlanta and California, describes the system as a modern alternative to traditional transit such as light rail, streetcars and people movers. Supporters said it could dramatically improve mobility in one of South Florida's fastest-growing areas, connecting the airport to the convention center and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept functions like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without getting stuck in traffic or making multiple intermediate stops.

Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying about four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, bypassing traffic congestion entirely. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. While the company has not disclosed a specific price tag, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail discussions that carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could potentially come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie advances land transfer for new Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
hero.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange coming to the Turnpike.
hero.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance in June to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Midway Road. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange will help close a significant gap between entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website for the project, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting. The partial interchange is still in the design phase, according to the FDOT website. Erin Scheumeister, a Port St. Lucie resident, said she believes the expansion is necessary despite the construction inconvenience.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock to close Sunday for $3 million renovation, doubling slip capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long renovation that will nearly double its capacity.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The $3 million project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually. During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will continue running during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the dock for boarding passengers. Kuyrkendall acknowledged the dock's current limitations, particularly on busy weekends when finding spots can be difficult.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue 2 boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded Wednesday to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1, thanks to a quick response from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies and a critical decision to wear life jackets. The Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded, with both occupants ending up in the water when their boat went down.

The boaters were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Delray Beach area golf training center delayed 3 months, costs owner $90,000 after contractor issues
cards.teaser: Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, said the project was delayed by three months after problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, faced significant delays and costs after hiring a contractor to prepare the space. Instead of opening in April as scheduled, the project was delayed three months when work had to be redone. Molen estimated the issues cost him approximately $90,000, not including lost revenue during the delays or the added expense of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. He said the work involved double paying on electricians, HVAC, and drywall.

Molen worked with Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, an organization warning property and business owners to thoroughly vet contractors before hiring them. Founder David Allan estimates 25% to 35% of homeowners and property owners in Palm Beach County face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. According to Allan, the most common contractor complaints in the county involve roofing, windows, and air conditioning work. Despite the setbacks, Tee Box's grand opening is set for July 17.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets roof repaired, lien removed after turning to WPTV for help
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, came to WPTV's Let's Hear It event in Boynton Beach after months of frustration with Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. McCoy made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000 and said he was mostly satisfied with the work, except for two holes left unfinished on the back of his home. After reporting the issues, McCoy said the company stopped responding. Screenshots he shared with WPTV show that between Jan. 10 and Feb. 5, he called, texted and emailed the company multiple times. Letters from Gulfeagle Supply subsequently arrived at his home warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien against his property. The lien document stated Gulfeagle Supply furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing but was not paid for those supplies.

WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey visited Seabreeze Roofing and spoke with the owner. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, lifting the lien from his home. McCoy also learned the contractor would send someone back to repair the two problem areas on his roof. About an hour after McCoy received the waiver, he sent WPTV a photo showing crews working on his roof to finish the job.

cards.headline: Martin County to open online portal in August for manufactured home repair funding
cards.teaser: Senate Bill 594 expands access to $167 million in state SHIP funding for manufactured home emergency repairs and storm-hardening retrofits. Martin County expects to dedicate about 75% of its annual SHIP funding to eligible mobile and manufactured homeowners.
cards.body:
Martin County will open an online portal in August for manufactured and mobile home owners to apply for emergency repairs and storm-hardening retrofits under Senate Bill 594, which took effect July 1st. The law makes $167 million in state affordable housing funding available to eligible homeowners. According to Julie Stellatos with Martin County Human Services, approximately 75 percent of the county's annual SHIP funding, typically between $1 million and $1.5 million, can now be directed toward manufactured homeowners. Applicants can complete an online application or call the Martin County office to request one be mailed to them. Stellatos emphasized that funding operates on a first-come, first-served basis.

The legislative action followed an investigation into an EF-3 tornado that destroyed 138 homes at Spanish Lakes Country Club Community in Fort Pierce and killed six residents. The investigation found nearly 700,000 of Florida's more than 1 million mobile and manufactured homes were built before current federal safety standards and cannot withstand modern storms. Among the five counties in the viewing area, Okeechobee County is updating its local housing assistance plan to offer lot rent, rehabilitation and emergency repair assistance. St. Lucie County is awaiting final state guidance before announcing its application process. Indian River County will present the changes to its board on August 18th, with a September 30th deadline to submit its plan to the state.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July fireworks and pool party at country club
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse will host Independence Day celebrations on July 4 with a pool party, barbecue buffet and fireworks at 9 p.m.
hero.body:
North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County. The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle programs through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs through September during peak sea turtle nesting season. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these programs are designed to help visitors learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. Loggerhead Marinelife Center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Democratic PAC Engage Y'All endorses 22 Florida candidates in legislative, congressional races
hero.body:
A Democratic political action committee has announced support for 22 candidates running across Florida this election cycle, betting that recent special election victories show the party can compete in districts traditionally considered Republican strongholds. Engage Y'All endorsed two congressional candidates, 16 legislative hopefuls, and four local candidates as part of a strategy to expand Democratic representation in the state.

The congressional endorsements include Pia Dandiya, who is running for the open Florida's 22nd Congressional District seat, and Nicole Locklin, who is challenging Republican U.S. Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart in Florida's 26th Congressional District. In state Senate races, the PAC backed Lauren Donahoo against Republican state Sen. Corey Simon in Senate District 2 and Ashley Gantt in Senate District 34, which opened after Democratic state Sen. Shevrin Jones decided to run for Congress. The PAC also endorsed 14 candidates in state House races across Florida, with 11 of those races currently held by Republicans. House endorsements span districts throughout the state and include Jane Aman, Lucai Baez-Geller, Darryl Block, Daniel Cicirelli, Kyandra Darling, Michelle DeJesus, Jared Fox, Eric Gray, August Mangeney, Justin Mendoza-Routt, May Thach, John Taylor, Samuel Vilchez Santiago, and Ingrid Wadsworth.

Beyond legislative races, the PAC supported Dee Galery for Palm Coast City Council, Linsey Grove for St. Petersburg City Council, Susanne Pena for Orange County School Board, and Victor Sims for Polk County School Board. Katherine Jackson, senior communications advisor for the PAC, said the endorsements represent "leaders across the state who are rising to meet this moment for the people they seek to represent." The slate of candidates reflects demographic diversity, with 59 percent women, 50 percent people of color, and 86 percent from millennial and Generation Z age groups.

Engage Y'All was founded last year by Democratic congressional candidate Gay Valimont following her special election campaign against now-U.S. Rep. Jimmy Patronis in Florida's 1st Congressional District. Though Patronis won that race with nearly 57 percent of the vote, Valimont significantly improved her performance compared to a previous attempt against the prior incumbent. She is challenging Patronis again in 2026. The PAC's approach focuses on persuading Democrats that they can succeed in districts many view as unlikely Democratic wins. The organization has already helped flip two legislative seats to Democratic control, with state Rep. Emily Gregory from Palm Beach County and state Sen. Brian Nathan from Tampa winning races with PAC support. The group also assisted Democrat Eileen Higgins in winning the Miami Mayor race. Engage Y'All accumulated substantial resources during a Panhandle special election last year.

cards.headline: Democratic first responder Bernard Taylor raises $563,000 in second quarter for Florida Congressional District 21 race
cards.teaser: EMT and paramedic Bernard Taylor announced his campaign collected just under $563,000 in the second quarter, with more than 25,000 individual donations averaging $22 each.
cards.body:
Democratic first responder Bernard Taylor raised just under $563,000 in the second quarter for his challenge against Republican U.S. Rep. Brian Mast in Florida's 21st Congressional District. Taylor, an EMT and paramedic, reported receiving more than 25,000 individual donations averaging $22 each from April 1 to June 30. His campaign declined all corporate PAC money and special-interest donations, with more than 93% of contributions coming through mobile devices and roughly 41% routed through digital fundraising platform ActBlue. Taylor had previously raised just $32,500 after filing for the race in April 2025, according to Federal Election Commission records.

A fourth-generation Floridian, Taylor is running on a platform prioritizing affordable healthcare access, educational investment, job creation, housing affordability, and environmental protection. He said his work in emergency medical services exposed him to the real-world consequences of rising costs and limited healthcare options facing families across the coastal district, which stretches from Royal Palm Beach in Palm Beach County north through Martin and St. Lucie counties. About 57.5% of voters in the district voted for President Donald Trump in 2024 under new congressional boundaries enacted by Gov. Ron DeSantis and the GOP-dominated Legislature in April. Taylor faces a primary opponent in U.S. Coast Guard veteran James Martin, who entered the second quarter with nearly $307,000 raised. Other candidates include independent Alexander Cooke and write-in candidate David Fabrikant. Mast entered April with more than $2.5 million in cash on hand.

cards.headline: Former Florida Democratic Party Chair Allison Tant endorses Charlie Crist for St. Petersburg Mayor
cards.teaser: State Rep. Allison Tant announced support for former Governor Charlie Crist's campaign for St. Petersburg Mayor based on a decadeslong political relationship.
cards.body:
Allison Tant, former Chair of the Florida Democratic Party, is endorsing Charlie Crist's campaign for St. Petersburg Mayor based on their decades-long political relationship. Tant said she has known Crist through his service as state Senator, Governor, and Congressman. "I'm delighted to see him take this chance to return to public service. He shows up, he listens, he rolls up his sleeves and takes action to address the work of caring for others and his community," Tant said. Crist announced the endorsement Thursday, praising Tant for her longtime advocacy for students, families, and Floridians with disabilities and her service as former Chair of the Florida Democratic Party.

Tant joins a growing slate of Democratic leaders endorsing Crist's campaign against incumbent Mayor Ken Welch. The group includes U.S. Rep. Lois Frankel, former U.S. Reps. Cheri Bustos of Illinois and Matt Cartwright of Pennsylvania, state Sen. Darryl Rouson, former state Rep. Ben Diamond, and state Rep. Frank Peterman. The St. Petersburg Mayor's race is nonpartisan but has drawn significant attention from Democratic elected officials and activists as Crist and Welch compete for support among the city's left-leaning voter base. City Council Member Brandi Gabbard is also polling with double-digit support ahead of several other candidates vying for the seat.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Police union backs Belinda Keiser in Florida Congressional District 22 race
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach Police Benevolent Association endorsed Republican congressional candidate Belinda Keiser's campaign for the open Florida's 22nd Congressional District seat.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Police Benevolent Association has endorsed Republican congressional candidate Belinda Keiser for Florida's 22nd Congressional District. John Kazanjian, President of the Palm Beach Police Benevolent Association, said Keiser is a strong law and order conservative who understands the importance of protecting and supporting law enforcement. Kazanjian called on association members, their friends and families, and all Palm Beach County citizens who respect strong law enforcement to vote for Keiser. He said that in Washington, she will advocate for law enforcement needs, defend the rule of law, hold criminals accountable, and keep communities safe.

Keiser, Vice Chancellor of Keiser University, said she is deeply honored by the endorsement and acknowledged that law enforcement put their lives on the line daily. She noted that Keiser University made it a priority to have the Multiple Interactive Learning Objective simulator available for criminal justice and homeland security students as hands-on training. Keiser said she will fight in Congress to ensure law enforcement have the resources, training, and support they need. She is one of seven Republicans who qualified for the open seat. A congressional map enacted this year by Gov. Ron DeSantis left the battleground seat with no natural incumbent. Under the new lines, about 55% of voters in Congressional District 22 supported Republican Donald Trump in the 2024 Presidential Election.

cards.headline: Tampa defense contractor TRAK TECOM supplies critical technology for F-35 fighter jets
cards.teaser: Tampa-based TRAK TECOM has specialized in designing RF assemblies and defense antenna systems for military and aerospace applications for more than 65 years.
cards.body:
TRAK TECOM, a Tampa-based company specializing in RF assemblies and defense antenna systems for over 65 years, supplies critical technologies for the F-35 Lightning II fighter jet. The company's engineers develop advanced RF microwave assemblies, circulators, multichannel switch filter banks, low-silhouette blade antennas, Ku/Ka SATCOM antennas, and up/down converters that enable the aircraft to communicate, share data, and maintain situational awareness in contested environments. These components are central to the F-35's operational capability rather than peripheral additions.

The F-35 program connects nearly 1,900 businesses nationwide, with more than 160 located in Florida and supporting over 30,000 jobs statewide. Florida generates an estimated $23 billion in economic impact from the F-35 supply chain. In the Tampa Bay region specifically, the program generates $150 million in annual economic impact and supports more than 700 direct jobs, including small businesses and veteran-owned suppliers. Nineteen nations have partnered with the United States to purchase and field the F-35, strengthening interoperability and collective defense. Recent Israeli F-35 operations demonstrate the platform's precision, survivability, and dominance in real-world combat.

cards.headline: Florida reports lowest residential arson rate in United States during July
cards.teaser: Florida averaged just 17.8 residential arson incidents statewide each year over the last five Julys, about one for every 586,000 homes, according to a new analysis of FBI crime data.
cards.body:
Florida has the nation's lowest rate of residential arson during July, according to a new analysis of FBI crime data. The study, conducted by Besroi Roofing and Siding using FBI Crime Data Explorer records from 2021 through 2025, found Florida averaged just 17.8 residential arson incidents statewide each July over the past five years, or about one for every 586,000 homes. Florida edged out New Jersey for the top spot and dramatically outperformed neighboring Georgia and Alabama, where residential arson rates were roughly four and 10 times higher, respectively. Florida's July residential arson rate is roughly one-sixth the national average, despite the state having the country's third-largest housing market.

The findings come as millions of Floridians prepare to celebrate Independence Day with backyard barbecues and fireworks. Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson and the Florida Forest Service reminded residents that even though drought conditions are easing, wildfire season continues and fireworks should be used responsibly.

cards.headline: New poll shows Floridians report declining patriotism ahead of Independence Day weekend
cards.teaser: A new Gallup poll found many Americans, including Floridians, report feeling less proud to be American, according to a report published Thursday.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card Body

Recent polling shows Floridians report declining patriotism ahead of the Independence Day weekend, according to a Gallup poll highlighted in Florida Politics. The timing coincides with the nation's preparation to celebrate its 250th Independence Day, when millions of Floridians are expected to gather for backyard barbecues and fireworks displays.

The poll results reflect shifting public sentiment as the country marks its semiquincentennial. Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson and the Florida Forest Service have spent the lead-up to the holiday reminding residents to use fireworks responsibly, noting that despite easing drought conditions, wildfire season remains a concern.

hero.headline: Four Martin County teens arrested after 14-year-old robbed at gunpoint
hero.teaser: Martin County deputies arrested four teenagers after a 14-year-old boy was robbed at gunpoint. The teens led deputies on a chase following the alleged robbery.
hero.body:
Four Martin County teenagers were arrested after a 14-year-old boy was robbed at gunpoint. The incident occurred on Thursday, prompting a response from Martin County deputies.

The teens led Martin County deputies on a chase following the alleged robbery. Deputies eventually apprehended all four suspects. The ages and identities of the arrested teens were not provided in available reports.

cards.headline: Person dies in fire on Southeast Cactus Trail in Hobe Sound
cards.teaser: A person died in a fire on Southeast Cactus Trail in Hobe Sound on Thursday.
cards.body: The fire was reported on Thursday evening. Authorities responded to the scene on Southeast Cactus Trail, where the victim was found deceased.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters were rescued after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday. Marine deputies said life jackets kept them afloat while help arrived.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1, thanks to a quick response from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets. The Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded, with both occupants ending up in the water when their boat went down.

The boaters were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances plan for Midway Road expansion and new Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a new partial interchange for the Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. According to Samples, the interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial interchange for the Turnpike is also still in the design phase. FDOT said the Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths, along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Zoning Commission recommends denial of data center near Arden and Saddle View Elementary
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend denial of Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

One of the central issues during Thursday's hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Board members said they were not presented with enough evidence to conclude the facility would meet that standard. Project developer Ernie Cox said he was disappointed by the board's recommendation but plans to use the feedback from Thursday's hearing to strengthen his case before county commissioners.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof fixed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, turned to WPTV for help after a roofing contractor left him with unfinished repairs and a lien on his home.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. McCoy made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000 but said he was mostly satisfied with the work except for two unfinished holes on the back side of his home. After reporting the problems, McCoy said the company stopped responding to his calls, texts, and emails, despite visiting their building multiple times between January 10 and early February.

McCoy's situation worsened when Gulfeagle Supply filed a nearly $7,000 lien against his home, claiming Seabreeze Roofing never paid for materials supplied to McCoy's property. Facing the prospect of hiring an attorney, McCoy turned to WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey. After Hussey spoke directly with Seabreeze Roofing's owner about the unpaid materials and lien, the situation quickly resolved. Within an hour, Hussey returned with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized. McCoy also learned the contractor would return to fix the two problem roof areas, with crews arriving about an hour after he received the waiver.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie advances $95 million Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange project
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie is moving forward with a major infrastructure initiative that includes a $95 million road widening project and a new partial interchange for Florida's Turnpike. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance that would transfer 7 acres of city land to the Florida Department of Transportation to support the interchange construction. The council is expected to vote on final approval of the land transfer at a future meeting.

The Midway Road Widening Project addresses congestion and safety concerns in the growing community. Currently, crews are focused on the first phase of construction, which expands the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. According to FDOT's project timeline, the second phase of widening from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. Beyond the road expansion, FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and designing the partial interchange, which is still in its planning stages.

City officials emphasize that the projects are essential for managing growth in Port St. Lucie. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for the city, noted that there is currently "a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike" in Port St. Lucie. He explained that the interchange aims to improve accessibility while preparing for both current and future population growth. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," Samples said.

The project has received mixed reactions from residents who experience the ongoing construction. While some find the work disruptive to their daily lives, most acknowledge its necessity. Local resident Erin Scheumeister said construction can be frustrating but expressed support for the expansion. "We definitely needed it to be expanded," she said. "It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." Beyond the roadway improvements, the Midway Road Widening Project will also include bike and pedestrian paths as well as sidewalks, adding multimodal transportation options for the community.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters were pulled from the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday after their small motorized boat took on water and sank. The pair survived because they wore life jackets.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel.

The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Driver held Port St. Lucie teens at gunpoint after Orbeez pellet shooting
cards.teaser: A driver held teens at gunpoint in Port St. Lucie after they shot Orbeez pellets at his car, according to police.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police say a driver confronted teens with a gun after the teens shot Orbeez pellets at his vehicle. The incident occurred in Port St. Lucie.

The driver held the teens at gunpoint following the pellet shooting. Police responded to the confrontation involving the teens and the armed driver.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce drug bust uncovers 60.5 grams of meth and 43.5 grams of MDMA
cards.teaser: Authorities seized trafficking amounts of methamphetamine and MDMA in a Fort Pierce bust.
cards.body:
Law enforcement in Fort Pierce seized 60.5 grams of methamphetamine and 43.5 grams of MDMA in a drug trafficking investigation. The quantities found meet trafficking thresholds under Florida law.

The bust occurred in Fort Pierce and resulted in the discovery of the trafficking stash. Authorities recovered both substances during the operation.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested on child pornography charges
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a Fort Pierce man on child pornography charges.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce man was taken into custody on child pornography charges, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. The arrest was announced by the sheriff's office.

The man faces charges related to child pornography. The sheriff's office conducted the investigation that led to the arrest in Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Endangered snail kites spotted in St. Lucie County community
cards.teaser: Endangered snail kites have been observed in a St. Lucie County community.
cards.body:
Endangered snail kites have made their way into a St. Lucie County community. The birds, which are protected under endangered species laws, were spotted by residents.

Snail kites are wetland birds that feed primarily on apple snails. Their presence in St. Lucie County indicates suitable habitat for the endangered species.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce officer dedicates career to helping homeless find hope
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce police officer has spent a lifetime of service helping homeless individuals find hope and resources.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce police officer has made helping the homeless a central part of his law enforcement career. The officer has dedicated years to connecting homeless individuals with resources and support.

The Fort Pierce officer works to provide hope and assistance to homeless people in the community. His efforts have focused on connecting vulnerable residents with services and pathways out of homelessness.

hero.headline: Two rescued after boat sinks in Indian River Lagoon
hero.teaser: Two boaters were rescued after their vessel sank in the Indian River Lagoon on Wednesday.
hero.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies and their decision to wear life jackets. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie expands Midway Road, plans Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a planned partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between current Turnpike entrances and exits in the city and is designed to accommodate growth over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial Turnpike interchange remains in the design phase. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Zoning board recommends denial of data center near Arden and Saddle View Elementary
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend that county commissioners deny Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach County Planning and Zoning Board unanimously voted Thursday to recommend denial of Project Tango, a proposed hyperscale AI data center planned near the Arden community and Saddle View Elementary School in western Palm Beach County. The recommendation followed a nearly five-hour public hearing at the Vista Center that drew more than 100 attendees, with more than 40 residents speaking during public comment. The proposed facility would be built approximately 1,100 feet from the Arden community and the recently opened Saddle View Elementary School. The project now heads to the Palm Beach County Commission, which will make the final decision during a July 15 public hearing.

One of the central issues during Thursday's hearing was how the project should be classified under the county's land development code. Board members questioned whether the proposed data center qualifies as light industrial or should instead be considered heavy industrial. Under county regulations, light industrial uses cannot create impacts beyond their property lines. Board members said they were not presented with enough evidence to conclude the facility would meet that standard. Residents raised concerns about potential health, safety, environmental and noise impacts. County commissioners are expected to consider both the planning staff's recommendation for approval and the Planning and Zoning Board's recommendation for denial when they make the final decision on July 15.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed, roof fixed after WPTV steps in
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran, said a roofing contractor left him with unfinished repairs and a lien on his home after he paid more than $17,000.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. McCoy made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000 but said he was mostly satisfied with the work except for two unfinished holes on the back of his home. When the contractor stopped responding to his calls, texts, and emails beginning in January, McCoy attempted to reach them in person multiple times without success.

McCoy's situation worsened when Gulfeagle Supply filed a nearly $7,000 lien against his home, claiming Seabreeze Roofing had not paid for materials supplied to McCoy's property. After WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey visited Seabreeze Roofing and spoke with the owner, she returned to McCoy's home within an hour with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized. The contractor also committed to fixing the two unfinished roof areas. About an hour after receiving the waiver, McCoy sent WPTV a photo showing crews back on his roof completing the repairs.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach airport transit proposal under consideration by county commissioners
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to the airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The elevated network of self-driving vehicles would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. The company describes the system as a modern alternative to traditional transit such as light rail, streetcars and people movers. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept is designed to function like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without getting stuck in traffic or making multiple intermediate stops.

Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying about four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. The system would bypass traffic congestion entirely, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail discussions that carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Tuesday's meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

cards.headline: Golf training center near Delray Beach delayed 3 months after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training center near Delray Beach, said problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space delayed the project by three months.
cards.body:
Tom Molen's dream of opening Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, was delayed three months after contractor problems forced extensive rework. Although the contractor was licensed, Molen said the work had to be redone, creating a costly domino effect that cost him approximately $90,000. That figure does not include revenue lost during the delays or the additional expense of hiring another contractor to fix the problems, including double payments to electricians, HVAC workers, and drywall contractors.

Molen worked with Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, an organization warning property and business owners to thoroughly vet contractors before hiring them. Founder David Allan estimates that 25 to 35 percent of homeowners and property owners in Palm Beach County face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. The most common contractor complaints in the county involve roofing, windows, and air conditioning work. After months of delays and repairs, Tee Box's grand opening is scheduled for July 17.
